title: Weighted perimeter, Gaussian isoperimetry and clusters
summary: Weighted perimeter for positive C¹ densities on finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, clusters and existence of minimizing clusters, the Gaussian model simplicial clusters and model profile with ∇²I_m = −L_A⁻¹, Ehrhard symmetrisation of sets of finite Gaussian perimeter, the Gaussian isoperimetric theorem with equality (half-spaces) and its two-cell cluster form, the Borell–Sudakov–Tsirelson inequality for every Gaussian law, Bobkov's inequality and its converse, median concentration of Lipschitz functions, and Ehrhard's inequality for convex sets.

layers.title: The standard Gaussian on the line and on Euclidean spaces

targets.name: gaussianIsoperimetricProfile
targets.statement: I : ℝ → ℝ, I(v) = φ(Φ⁻¹(v)) for 0 < v < 1 with Φ⁻¹(v) the quantile of gaussianReal 0 1, and I(v) = 0 otherwise.

api.name: profile_cdf
api.statement: I(Φ(s)) = φ(s) for every real s; Φ(Φ⁻¹(v)) = v on (0,1) and Φ⁻¹(Φ(s)) = s.

api.name: profile_one_sub
api.statement: I(1 − v) = I(v) for all v.

api.name: continuousOn_profile
api.statement: I is continuous on [0,1], positive on (0,1), zero at 0 and 1, maximal value φ(0) only at 1/2.

api.name: profile_deriv
api.statement: I is C^∞ on (0,1) with I′ = −Φ⁻¹ and I″ = −1/I; hence strictly concave on [0,1] and locally Lipschitz on (0,1).

tests.name: profile_endpoints

tests.name: profile_ode

tests.name: profile_normalization
tests.statement: The Cianchi–Fusco–Maggi–Pratelli profile e^{−Φ_CFMP⁻¹(r)²/2} equals √(2π)·I: at r = 1 − Φ(1) it is 0.606531 instead of 0.241971.

targets.name: stdGaussian_eq_map_add_prod
targets.statement: For a subspace F ⊆ E, addition F × F^⊥ → E carries stdGaussian F ⊗ stdGaussian F^⊥ to stdGaussian E; the orthogonal projection onto F carries γ_E to γ_F; γ_E({⟨x,ν⟩ < s}) = Φ(s) for unit ν; and γ_E = e^{−W}·volume with W(x) = ‖x‖²/2 + (n/2)log(2π).
hypotheses: E finite-dimensional real inner product space

tests.name: splitting_trivial
tests.statement: F = {0} gives γ_E = δ_0 ⊗ γ_E; the density at 0 in ℝ² is (2π)^{−1} = 0.159155.

targets.name: weightedVariation
targets.statement: For a C¹ weight W, open Ω ⊆ E and u ∈ L¹_loc(Ω): V_μ(u;Ω) = sup {∫_Ω u (div X − ⟨∇W,X⟩) e^{−W} dx : X smooth, compactly supported in Ω, ‖X‖ ≤ 1} ∈ [0,∞]. P_μ(U;Ω) = V_μ(χ_U;Ω), P_μ(U) = P_μ(U;E).
hypotheses: E finite-dimensional real inner product space, dim E = n ≥ 1
W : E → ℝ of class C¹

api.name: weightedPerimeter
api.statement: P_μ(U;Ω) = V_μ(χ_U;Ω).

api.name: weightedVariation_eq_sup_density_bounded
api.statement: V_μ(u;Ω) = sup ∫_Ω u div Y dx over C¹ (or smooth) Y compactly supported in Ω with ‖Y‖ ≤ e^{−W}.

api.name: weightedPerimeter_compl
api.statement: P_μ(E∖U;Ω) = P_μ(U;Ω); V_μ depends only on the a.e. class of u; P_μ(∅) = P_μ(E) = 0.

api.name: weightedVariation_mono
api.statement: Ω ⊆ Ω′ ⇒ V_μ(u;Ω) ≤ V_μ(u;Ω′); subadditive and absolutely homogeneous in u.

api.name: weightedVariation_add_const
api.statement: The weight W + c multiplies V_μ by e^{−c}; W = 0 gives the Euclidean variation of GeometricMeasureTheory G3.

api.name: weightedVariation_local_comparison
api.statement: For Ω′ with compact closure in Ω: (min e^{−W})|Du|(Ω′) ≤ V_μ(u;Ω′) ≤ (max e^{−W})|Du|(Ω′); V_μ(u;Ω) < ∞ ⇒ u ∈ BV_loc(Ω).

tests.name: euclidean_halfline
tests.statement: W = 0 on ℝ: P((0,∞)) = 1, P((0,1)) = 2; a half-plane of ℝ² has Euclidean perimeter ∞ but finite Gaussian perimeter.

tests.name: missing_drift_term
tests.statement: Without −⟨∇W,X⟩ the supremum gives ℝ under γ the value ∫|t| dγ = 0.797885 instead of 0 and is not complement invariant.

targets.name: weightedVariation_eq_lintegral
targets.statement: For u ∈ BV_loc(Ω) and open Ω′ ⊆ Ω, V_μ(u;Ω′) = ∫_{Ω′} e^{−W} d|Du|, defining V_μ(u;B) for Borel B; if U has locally finite perimeter in Ω (in particular if P_μ(U;Ω) < ∞), then P_μ(U;B) = μ^{n−1}(∂*U ∩ B) = μ^{n−1}(∂^M U ∩ B) for Borel B ⊆ Ω.

tests.name: null_modification
tests.statement: Removing the origin from ball(0,1) ⊂ ℝ² or adding a null dense set outside it leaves P_γ = 0.606531.

targets.name: weightedPerimeter_le_frontier
targets.statement: For Lebesgue-measurable U and open Ω, P_μ(U;Ω) ≤ μ^{n−1}(∂^M U ∩ Ω) ≤ μ^{n−1}(frontier U ∩ Ω); for open convex C and bounded Lipschitz domains, P_μ(C;Ω) = μ^{n−1}(∂C ∩ Ω); P_γ({⟨x,ν⟩ < s}) = φ(s) and P_γ(ball(0,r)) = (2π)^{−n/2} e^{−r²/2} n ω_n r^{n−1}.

targets.name: weightedVariation_lowerSemicontinuous
targets.statement: u_k → u in L¹_loc(Ω) ⇒ V_μ(u;Ω) ≤ liminf V_μ(u_k;Ω); if μ(E) < ∞, sets with sup P_μ(U_k) < ∞ have a subsequence converging in L¹(μ) to some U with P_μ(U) ≤ liminf P_μ(U_k).

locator.where: line 209–213; MilmanNeeman2022 line 939–947; Maggi2012 Proposition 12.15 and Theorem 12.26

tests.name: escaping_halfspaces
tests.statement: Under γ, {x_1 < k} → E with P_γ = φ(k) → 0.

tests.name: infinite_mass
tests.statement: Weight 0 on ℝ: (k,k+1) has perimeter 2 and no L¹ limit.

targets.name: integral_weightedDiv_eq_boundary
targets.statement: For U of locally finite perimeter and X ∈ C¹_c: ∫_U div_μ X dμ = ∫_{∂*U} ⟨X,ν_U⟩ dμ^{n−1}; the same for bounded C¹ X with bounded derivative and ⟨∇W,X⟩ ∈ L¹(μ) when μ(E) < ∞ and P_μ(U) < ∞; for γ and P_γ(U) < ∞, d/dt γ(U + tw)|_{t=0} = ∫_{∂*U} ⟨w,ν_U⟩ dγ^{n−1}.

locator.where: equations (3.1) and (3.3), line 705–708 and 758–761; Maggi2012 Theorem 15.9

tests.name: translation_sign
tests.statement: U = {x_1 < s}, w = e_1: derivative φ(s); an inner normal gives −φ(s).

targets.name: lintegral_weighted_coarea
targets.statement: (a) Lipschitz f, Borel g ≥ 0: ∫ g‖∇f‖ dμ = ∫_ℝ ∫_{f⁻¹(t)} g dμ^{n−1} dt; (b) u ∈ L¹_loc(Ω): V_μ(u;Ω) = ∫_ℝ P_μ({u > t};Ω) dt, and on Borel subsets for u ∈ BV_loc(Ω).

tests.name: radial
tests.statement: f = ‖x‖ on ℝ², μ = γ: both sides 1.000000.

tests.name: linear
tests.statement: u(t) = t on ℝ: ∫φ = 1 on both sides.

targets.name: gaussianPerimeter_cylinder
targets.statement: For a linear isometry equivalence T : E ≃ E′, P_γ(T U) = P_γ(U); for a subspace F and Lebesgue-measurable U ⊆ F, γ_E(U ⊕ F^⊥) = γ_F(U) and P_{γ_E}(U ⊕ F^⊥) = P_{γ_F}(U).

tests.name: halfplane_cylinder
tests.statement: F = ℝe_1 ⊂ ℝ², U = (−∞,s): φ(s) both sides.

targets.name: Cluster
targets.statement: A q-cluster (q ≥ 2) for μ is a q-tuple of Lebesgue-measurable, pairwise disjoint cells Ω_i with μ(E ∖ ⋃Ω_i) = 0 and P_μ(Ω_i) < ∞; total perimeter P_μ(Ω) = ½ Σ_i P_μ(Ω_i); measure vector μ(Ω) ∈ Δ^(q−1) when μ(E) = 1; equivalence up to null sets.

locator.where: line 57–67 and 697–702; Maggi2012 Part IV synopsis, line 716–725

api.name: Cluster.congr
api.statement: Equivalent clusters have equal total perimeter, measure vector and interfaces.

api.name: Cluster.perm
api.statement: Permuting cells gives a cluster with the same total perimeter and permuted measure vector.

api.name: Cluster.merge
api.statement: For q ≥ 3, merging Ω_i and Ω_j gives a (q−1)-cluster whose total perimeter drops by A_ij.

api.name: Cluster.perimeter_two
api.statement: For q = 2, P_μ(Ω) = P_μ(Ω_1) = P_μ(Ω_2).

api.name: Cluster.isometry
api.statement: A linear isometry carries γ-clusters to γ-clusters with the same total perimeter.

tests.name: three_intervals
tests.statement: Cells (−∞,a),(a,b),(b,∞) under γ on ℝ have total perimeter φ(a)+φ(b); without the factor ½ every interface is counted twice.

tests.name: trivial_cluster
tests.statement: (E, ∅) is a 2-cluster of total perimeter 0 with measure vector (1,0).

tests.name: infinite_perimeter_cell
tests.statement: (⋃_k (1/(2k+1),1/(2k)), complement) is not a cluster: the first cell has infinite perimeter; overlapping cells are excluded by disjointness.

tests.name: halfspace_pair
tests.statement: ({x_1 < s},{x_1 > s}) has total perimeter φ(s) = P_γ({x_1 < s}).

targets.name: Cluster.interface_decomposition
targets.statement: With Σ_ij = ∂*Ω_i ∩ ∂*Ω_j and A_ij = μ^{n−1}(Σ_ij): for S ⊆ {1..q}, μHE[n−1]-a.e. point of ∂*(⋃_S Ω_i) lies in some Σ_ij with i ∈ S, j ∉ S; a.e. point of ∂*Ω_i lies in exactly one Σ_ij; P_μ(Ω_i) = Σ_{j≠i} A_ij; P_μ(⋃_S Ω_i) = Σ_{i∈S,j∉S} A_ij; P_μ(Ω) = Σ_{i<j} A_ij; closure(∂*Ω_i) = closure(⋃_{j≠i} Σ_ij).

tests.name: set_equality_fails
tests.statement: Ω_1 = {x_2 < 0}, Ω_2 = half-annuli of radii in [2^{−2k−1},2^{−2k}), Ω_3 the rest of the upper half-plane: 0 ∈ ∂*Ω_1 but 0 ∉ ∂*Ω_2 ∪ ∂*Ω_3.

targets.name: Cluster.posDef_interfaceForm
targets.statement: If μ(E) = 1 and μ(Ω) ∈ int Δ^(q−1), the interface graph is connected and L_A is positive definite on E^(q−1).
hypotheses: μ(Ω) in the relative interior of the simplex

tests.name: chain
tests.statement: Three intervals: ⟨a,L_A a⟩ = φ(a)(a_1−a_2)² + φ(b)(a_2−a_3)², zero on E^(2) only at 0.

targets.name: isoperimetricProfile
targets.statement: For μ(E) = 1, q ≥ 2, v ∈ Δ^(q−1): I_μ^(q−1)(v) = inf {P_μ(Ω) : Ω a q-cluster with μ(Ω) = v}; a cluster is μ-minimizing when P_μ(Ω) = I_μ^(q−1)(μ(Ω)); I^(q−1) = I_γ^(q−1); I^(0)(1) = 0.

api.name: isoperimetricProfile_lt_top
api.statement: I_μ^(q−1)(v) < ∞ via concentric annuli.

api.name: isoperimetricProfile_perm
api.statement: Invariant under simultaneous permutation of coordinates; 0 at vertices.

api.name: isoperimetricProfile_le_face
api.statement: I_μ^(q−1)(v) ≤ I_μ^(|J|−1)(v_J) when v vanishes outside J.

tests.name: halfplane_failure
tests.statement: For ρ(x,y) = c(1+y²)exp(−x²(1+y²)⁴) the only half-plane {x<t} of measure 1/2 has infinite perimeter; balls and the symmetric slab {|x|<a} of measure 1/2 give finiteness.

targets.name: exists_isMinimizing_cluster
targets.statement: If μ(E) = 1, then for every q ≥ 2 and v ∈ Δ^(q−1) there is a μ-minimizing q-cluster with measure vector v.

tests.name: gaussian_half
tests.statement: q = 2, γ, v = (1/2,1/2): a minimizer exists; Layer 7 identifies it as a half-space through 0.

tests.name: infinite_mass
tests.statement: Weight 0 on ℝ: (k,k+1) is minimizing with no L¹ limit.

layers.title: Model simplicial clusters and the model profile

targets.name: modelCluster
targets.statement: On E^(q−1) = {x ∈ ℝ^q : Σx_i = 0}: Ω^m_i = {x : x_i > x_j ∀ j ≠ i}; x + Ω^m; Σ^m_ij = {x : x_i = x_j ≥ x_k ∀k}; A^m_ij(x) = γ_{q−1}^{q−2}(x + Σ^m_ij).

api.name: modelCluster_isCluster
api.statement: x + Ω^m is a γ-cluster of open convex polyhedral cones with interfaces x + Σ^m_ij and normals n_ij = (e_j − e_i)/√2.

api.name: modelInterfaceArea_pos
api.statement: A^m_ij(x) > 0 and P_γ(x + Ω^m) = Σ_{i<j} A^m_ij(x).

api.name: modelConormal_sum
api.statement: Each codimension-two face lies on exactly three interfaces with conormals (2e_k − e_i − e_j)/√6 summing to 0.

api.name: modelInterfaceArea_eq
api.statement: A^m_ij(x) = φ(⟨n_ij,x⟩)·γ_{n_ij^⊥}(π_ij x + Σ^m_ij).

tests.name: one_cell
tests.statement: q = 1: E^(0) = {0}, the one-cell cluster has perimeter 0.

targets.name: simplicialCluster
targets.statement: For 2 ≤ q ≤ n+1 and pairwise equidistant p_1..p_q ∈ E: Ω_i = {y : ‖y − p_i‖ < ‖y − p_j‖ ∀ j ≠ i}.

api.name: simplicialCluster_eq_image
api.statement: Every simplicial cluster is ι(x + Ω^m) ⊕ (range ι)^⊥ for a linear isometric embedding ι : E^(q−1) → E and x ∈ E^(q−1), and conversely.

api.name: simplicialCluster_cones
api.statement: Cells are open convex cones with apex the circumcentre; invariant under scaling the centres.

api.name: simplicialCluster_measure
api.statement: γ(Ω_i) = γ_{q−1}(x + Ω^m_i) and P_γ(Ω) = P_γ(x + Ω^m).

tests.name: two_centres
tests.statement: q = 2 gives complementary half-spaces: measures (Φ(s),1−Φ(s)), perimeter φ(s).

tests.name: equilateral
tests.statement: q = 3 in ℝ²: three 120° sectors, measures 1/3, perimeter 0.598413.

tests.name: collinear
tests.statement: Centres 0,1,2 in ℝ give a 3-cluster that is not simplicial.

targets.name: modelMeasureMap_diffeomorph
targets.statement: Ψ(x) = γ_{q−1}(x + Ω^m) is C^∞, injective, with image int Δ^(q−1) and derivative −L_{A^m(x)}/√2 on E^(q−1), invertible; Ψ is a diffeomorphism onto int Δ^(q−1).

tests.name: tie
tests.statement: y − x = (1,1,−2) lies in no open cell; the maximal-coordinate argument still gives Ψ_1(y) < Ψ_1(x).

targets.name: modelProfile
targets.statement: I_m^(q−1)(v) = P_γ(Ψ⁻¹(v) + Ω^m) = Σ_{i<j} A^m_ij(Ψ⁻¹(v)) on int Δ^(q−1); I_m^(0)(1) = 0. For n ≥ q − 1 every simplicial q-cluster in E with measure vector v has perimeter I_m^(q−1)(v), and one exists for each interior v.
hypotheses: n ≥ q − 1 for the transport statement

api.name: modelProfile_perm
api.statement: Invariant under permuting coordinates.

api.name: modelProfile_pos
api.statement: I_m^(q−1) > 0 on int Δ^(q−1).

tests.name: wrong_point
tests.statement: Evaluating at v − (1/q,…,1/q) instead of Ψ⁻¹(v) gives 0.355065 at v = (Φ(1),1−Φ(1)) instead of 0.241971.

targets.name: modelProfile_continuous_face
targets.statement: I_m^(q−1) is C^∞ on int Δ^(q−1), extends continuously to Δ^(q−1), and I_m^(q−1)(v) = I_m^(|J|−1)(v_J) on the face Δ_J, 0 < |J| < q.

targets.name: modelProfile_hessian
targets.statement: On int Δ^(q−1): ∇I_m = Ψ⁻¹/√2, ∇²I_m = −(L_{A^m}∘Ψ⁻¹)⁻¹ on E^(q−1), and −tr[(∇²I_m)⁻¹] = 2 I_m.

tests.name: conormal_terms
tests.statement: Keeping one apex term (2π)^{−1}⟨w,η⟩ = 0.159155⟨w,η⟩ breaks ∇I_m = 0 at the symmetric point.

targets.name: isoperimetricProfile_le_modelProfile
targets.statement: For n ≥ q − 1 and v ∈ Δ^(q−1): I^(q−1)(v) ≤ I_m^(q−1)(v).

tests.name: low_dimension
tests.statement: n = 1, q = 3: the three-interval cluster with measures 1/3 has perimeter 0.727200; the statement is not claimed.

targets.name: perimeter_real_locallyFinite_structure
targets.statement: For an open interval J ⊆ ℝ and U with locally finite perimeter in J: T = ∂^M U ∩ J is locally finite, equals ∂*U ∩ J, U ∩ J is a.e. a union of open intervals with endpoints T, and P_μ(U;B) = Σ_{t ∈ T∩B} e^{−W(t)}.
hypotheses: W : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹

tests.name: accumulating
tests.statement: ⋃(1/(2k+1),1/(2k)) is not of locally finite perimeter near 0.

targets.name: shift_interval_perimeter_lt
targets.statement: For −∞ < a < b < ∞ with a + b ≥ 0 and a < a′ < b′ ≤ ∞ with γ¹((a′,b′)) = γ¹((a,b)): φ(a′) + φ(b′) < φ(a) + φ(b); symmetric for left shifts when a + b ≤ 0.

targets.name: gaussianPerimeter_real_ge
targets.statement: Every Lebesgue-measurable U ⊆ ℝ satisfies P_γ(U) ≥ I(γ¹(U)), with equality iff γ¹(U) ∈ {0,1} or U is a.e. (−∞,s) or (s,∞).

tests.name: ae_halfline
tests.statement: (−∞,0) ∪ ℚ attains equality: the characterization is up to null sets.

layers.title: Gaussian symmetrisation of sets of finite Gaussian perimeter

targets.name: gaussianSymmetral
targets.statement: For a subspace F of dimension k ≥ 1, unit u ∈ F and Lebesgue-measurable U: U_x = {y ∈ F : x + y ∈ U}, v_U(x) = γ_F(U_x) for x ∈ F^⊥, S_{F,u}(U) = {x + y : Φ(⟨y,u⟩) < v_U(x)}; for F = ℝe, u = e it is the Ehrhard symmetral S_e(U).

locator.where: line 543–552 (mirrored superlevel convention); Ehrhard1983 Définition 1.1, line 117–129

api.name: gaussianSymmetral_measure
api.statement: S_{F,u}(U) is Lebesgue measurable, v_{S(U)} = v_U a.e., γ(S_{F,u}(U)) = γ(U).

api.name: gaussianSymmetral_mono
api.statement: U ⊆ U′ ⇒ S(U) ⊆ S(U′); a.e.-equal sets have a.e.-equal symmetrals; S is idempotent.

api.name: gaussianSymmetral_isometry
api.statement: For a linear isometry T with T(F) = F, T(u) = u: S(T U) = T S(U).

api.name: gaussianSymmetral_halfSpace
api.statement: {⟨x,u⟩ < a} is fixed; null sets go to ∅, conull sets to E.

tests.name: null_line

tests.name: sloped_line

tests.name: vertical_boundary

targets.name: sectionMeasure_bvLoc
targets.statement: For P_γ(U) < ∞, n ≥ 2, unit e: v_U ∈ BV_loc(e^⊥), ∫_B e^{−W_{e^⊥}} d|Dv_U| ≤ P_γ(U; B ⊕ ℝe) for Borel B, and the absolutely continuous part of Dv_U has density −Σ_t φ(t) ν_U^⊥/|⟨ν_U,e⟩| at good z, its singular part carried by the null projection of {⟨ν_U,e⟩ = 0}.

tests.name: tilted

targets.name: subgraphSet
targets.statement: For continuous f : E → [0,1]: A_f = {(x,y) ∈ E × ℝ : Φ(y) < f(x)} in the L²-product inner product space E × ℝ. Then γ(A_f) = ∫ f dγ_E, and for locally Lipschitz f the frontier is the graph of Φ⁻¹∘f over {0 < f < 1} with γ^n(frontier A_f) = ∫ √(I(f)² + ‖∇f‖²) dγ_E.

targets.statement: For locally Lipschitz f : E → [0,1]: I(∫ f dγ) ≤ ∫ √(I(f)² + ‖∇f‖²) dγ, with equality for constants and for Φ(α⟨x,ν⟩ + β); conversely the inequality for all Lipschitz f implies the Minkowski-content inequality of 8.2 for closed A.
